about: Dolin is one of the great old houses of the French Alps, best known for its Vermouth de Chambéry, the only French vermouth with its own appellation. The house dates to 1821, when the distiller Joseph Chavasse began making génépy and other liqueurs from Alpine plants; he settled in Chambéry in 1830. Since 1905 the company has belonged to the Sevez family, now in its fifth generation, and it remains independent.

Génépy, or génépi, is the mountain liqueur of Savoie, made from small artemisias, wormwood relatives that grow high in the Alps. Le Chamois is Dolin’s oldest recipe, unchanged since 1821. Herbs from local growers, picked in summer and led by Artemisia mutellina, are macerated and then distilled in the house’s old copper alembic, and the liqueur is bottled at 45%.

It has a gentle sweetness and a heady herbal character, with chamomile, sage and mint. In Savoie it is the classic glass after a fondue, served neat at cellar temperature in a small tulip glass; it is also refreshing on the rocks or with tonic, and bartenders use it in place of Chartreuse in classic Alpine-leaning cocktails.
